clue.text: WI place tea maker in as well

indicators.note: the tea maker is placed inside the word for 'as well'

parts.note: as well means too
a tea bag makes a cup of tea

explanation.surface: Someone in the West Indies setting up a kettle as well.
explanation.walkthrough: WI is the standard abbreviation for the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, half of the nation of Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: He wrote history for a century covered by emperor

indicators.note: the century piece is enclosed inside the emperor's name

parts.note: Titus was a Roman emperor
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A historian writing a hundred years of an emperor's reign.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was the Roman historian of the Annals and Histories.

clue.text: Campaign vigorously to make pub standard around street

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: the standard is wrapped around the abbreviation for street

parts.note: a norm is a standard

explanation.surface: A local pressure group fighting hard to get a pub built to code near the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To barnstorm is to tour making rousing political speeches.

clue.text: Stick dummy up

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mug is a fool or dummy

explanation.surface: An instruction to fix a ventriloquist's dummy in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum is an adhesive, used to stick things together.

clue.text: Putting away mockery

explanation.surface: Eating greedily while being jeered at.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting away food greedily is scoffing it; scoffing is also derisive scorn.

clue.text: 16 across reap crop in Dijon perhaps

explanation.surface: Harvesting a French condiment crop as a test of competence.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: cutting the mustard plants grown for Dijon mustard. Both phrases mean meeting the required standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean to reach the expected standard; literally, harvesting mustard is reaping the crop.

clue.text: Musical instruments produce note in equivalent of English outside

parts.note: French is a language standing where English would, and it tells us to translate the next word into it

indicators.note: the note is placed inside the foreign word for outside

parts.note: hors is the French word for outside, as in hors de combat

explanation.surface: Orchestral brass making a sound that matches English music from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' is a link word. HORS is French for outside, with N inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: French horns are coiled brass instruments of the orchestra.

clue.text: Robin merrily set in band

indicators.note: merrily suggests the letters of the name are tossed about

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's merry men setting up a group.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the phrase IN ORB: an orb is a ring or band, so a jewel set in a band is in orb.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a circle or ring, so something mounted in a ring is in orb.

clue.text: It cuts foul emissions from car in Grand Prix

indicators.note: the car's name goes inside the Grand Prix abbreviation

parts.note: the Astra is a Vauxhall car model

explanation.surface: Exhaust controls fitted to a racing car at a Grand Prix.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas trap is a bend in a drain that blocks smells from sewers.

clue.text: In saucer a microcosm of potter's art

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words saucer a microcosm

explanation.surface: A single saucer sums up the whole craft of the potter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramics is the art of making pottery from fired clay.

clue.text: Player's lined up in this?

parts.note: reads like a sportsman in a team line-up, but Player's is a brand of smokes kept in rows in a holder

explanation.walkthrough: Player's was a famous British brand of cigarettes, so the capital P is the giveaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim box holding smokes in a neat row; Player's was a well-known British tobacco brand.

clue.text: Rock band in hills, no great shakes

indicators.note: the band's name goes inside the word for hills

parts.note: tors are rocky hills on moorland
REM was an American rock band

explanation.surface: A rock group playing on the moors, unimpressively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No great shakes' usually means mediocre; here it means small shakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremors are small quakes, minor shudders rather than big earthquakes.

clue.text: It requires basic strength — Old English? — not exactly

definitions.text: It requires basic strength — Old English? — not exactly

indicators.note: not exactly says the letters given are not in their exact order

explanation.surface: A remark that some feat needs raw brawn, an English tradition, or not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: The sport is Scottish, not Old English, hence 'not exactly' in the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a heavy pole end over end at Highland games is a test of raw strength.

clue.text: Like paparazzi from Sun, it verily was disturbing

indicators.note: disturbing suggests the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A tabloid photographer from the Sun truly caused a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Paparazzi pry into celebrities' private lives in an intrusive manner.

clue.text: Speak bluntly of hot mother dancing on board

indicators.note: the dancing letters are put on board, inside the vessel's name

parts.note: to board is to go aboard a ship

indicators.note: dancing makes these letters move into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A heated mother dancing on a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot from the hip is to speak or act impulsively and directly.

clue.text: Chart collapse of apartheid

indicators.note: collapse suggests the word falls apart and is rebuilt

explanation.surface: A graph showing the end of the South African regime.
explanation.definitionFit: The hit parade is the chart of best-selling records.

clue.text: 5 down: what diver's itching to do?

explanation.surface: A diver with an itch surfacing to deal with it.
explanation.walkthrough: A diver who itches would come up to scratch; the phrase also means reach the required standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean to meet the expected standard; literally, a diver surfaces to relieve an itch.

clue.text: Involving woman in deception, he may provide some slack

indicators.note: involving means the deception wraps round the woman

parts.note: a con is a deception
Alma is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man who drags a woman into a deceit may give her some leeway.
explanation.walkthrough: Slack is coal dust, so a coal delivery man supplies it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack is small coal, which the coal merchant delivers.

clue.text: Flailing banshee's one old hat

indicators.note: flailing suggests the letters thrash about into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A wailing spirit flailing about is now out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is someone past their prime, no longer fashionable.

clue.text: Senior officers strangely cavalierish about bringer of war

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the war god's name
strangely says the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: Mars is the Roman god of war; Holst calls Mars the Bringer of War

explanation.surface: Top brass behaving with odd arrogance towards a warmonger.
explanation.definitionFit: An air vice-marshal is a senior RAF rank.

clue.text: Frenchman and wife begin again

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name

explanation.surface: A French husband and wife making a fresh start.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to restart or resume something.

clue.text: Nelson taking ship of the French

parts.note: to ship a crew is to engage them aboard, as to man is to crew
de la is French for of the

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson capturing a French vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Mandela was the South African leader.

clue.text: Cleared bats to end innings

indicators.note: bats in the sense of crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cricket ground cleared of bats so the innings can close.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a captain may declare, ending the team's innings early.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket captain closes an innings voluntarily by declaring.

clue.text: Manage without last policeman

indicators.note: without last means the word for manage loses its final letter

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Getting by without the final officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cop is slang for a police officer.

clue.text: One that's only just matched

parts.note: reads like something barely equal, but means someone recently paired in marriage

explanation.definitionFit: A person who has recently married has only just been paired up.

clue.text: Bad feeling observed around Poland

indicators.note: the word for observed goes around the country abbreviation

parts.note: seen means observed
PL is the international code for Poland

explanation.surface: Resentment noticed all over Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen is ill temper or resentment.
